issues.description: The study design involves participants interacting in pairs during the collaborative recall phase, meaning their memory reports will influence each other. However, the analysis plan proposes using a standard two-factor ANOVA on individual participant data. Analyzing nested data (individuals within interacting dyads) with standard ANOVA violates the assumption of independence, leading to artificially deflated standard errors and inflated Type I error rates. A multilevel model or dyadic analysis (e.g., Actor-Partner Interdependence Model or analyzing pair-level means) is required.
issues.quote: The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels (three groups of methods of reducing memory conformity and the control group).

issues.description: The procedure states that participants who correctly guess the study's hypotheses will be excluded. However, the 'Extended warning' intervention explicitly includes 'an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception.' Therefore, participants in this specific condition are directly told the purpose of the study and are highly likely to guess the hypotheses. Excluding them would systematically eliminate valid participants from this experimental group, destroying random assignment and severely biasing the results.
issues.quote: If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis... [Extended warning includes] an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception.

issues.description: The 'Demonstration and motivation' condition involves an interactive DRM task, writing words on a worksheet, receiving direct feedback from the experimenter, and listening to a podcast. In contrast, the other conditions (and the control) only involve listening to a 7-minute podcast. This introduces severe confounds regarding time-on-task, cognitive load, and experimenter interaction. Any differences observed could be due to these factors rather than the specific content of the intervention.
issues.quote: Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback... the experimenter will give the following information... Afterwards, the participants will be motivated... In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills...

issues.description: The introduction explicitly hypothesizes that the interventions will be effective specifically for participants who are aware of the discrepancies between their own memory and the co-witness misinformation. However, the methods and analysis plan do not include any measure of discrepancy awareness. Without measuring this, the researchers cannot test their stated theoretical mechanism.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.description: The authors note that during the discussion, a partner might provide an answer consistent with the original material, meaning no misinformation is delivered for that item. They state this 'will not be classified as misleading,' but fail to specify how this affects the within-subjects ANOVA. If an item is dropped, the number of items varies across participants. If it is kept but coded differently, the ANOVA structure changes. This ambiguity allows for undisclosed analytic flexibility.
issues.quote: However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen... the situation will not be classified as misleading... participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all... will be excluded from the analyses.

issues.subcategory: Inflated Type I error from multiple ANOVAs
issues.description: The analysis plan states that the researchers will run ANOVAs on four different indices derived from the open-ended test (correct answers, misinformation answers, other answers, overall answers). Running multiple ANOVAs on correlated dependent variables without applying a correction for multiple comparisons (e.g., Bonferroni, Holm) inflates the family-wise Type I error rate.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers.

issues.description: The analysis plan proposes using the DRM procedure results as a predictor of the MORI technique results. However, the DRM procedure is only administered to one of the four experimental groups ('Demonstration and motivation'). It is impossible to use this as a general predictor across the entire sample, and the text does not specify that this exploratory analysis is restricted to that single group.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.description: The authors describe a detailed coding scheme for categorizing discussion answers as 'disputed' or 'non-disputed.' However, this variable is completely absent from the subsequent analysis plan. It is unclear how or if this categorization will be used to test hypotheses or explore the data.
issues.quote: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions... we will categorize participants’ answers into two groups: “disputed” and “non-disputed”.

issues.description: The exclusion criteria state that individuals will be excluded if they guess the hypothesis or are not exposed to co-witness details. However, because participants are tested in pairs, it is not stated whether excluding one participant automatically results in the exclusion of their partner. If partners are retained, the dyadic structure is broken, which complicates any dyadic analysis or matching.
issues.quote: If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size.

issues.description: There is a critical typo in the introduction where the authors state that producing the same results 'does mean' the mechanisms are the same, when the context of the sentence clearly implies 'does not mean.' This creates a logical contradiction in their theoretical justification.
issues.quote: ...even if they produce the same results, this does mean that the mechanisms by which the were effective are always the same.

issues.description: The proposed interventions, particularly the 'Extended warning,' consist of multiple distinct components (e.g., warning of error, lecture on misinformation, source monitoring instructions, normative information, and enlightenment of deception). If the intervention is effective, the bundled design makes it impossible to determine which specific component (or combination of components) drove the effect.
issues.quote: In particular, the following ideas were included... a clear warning... an extensive lecture... information about the possibility of confusing sources... information that many people do... an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception.

issues.subcategory: Mismatch between DRM and memory conformity
issues.description: The 'Demonstration and motivation' condition uses the DRM paradigm to demonstrate memory fallibility. However, the DRM paradigm induces false memories through internal semantic activation, whereas memory conformity involves social suggestibility and source monitoring errors. Demonstrating semantic false memories may not effectively inoculate participants against social misinformation, representing a mismatch in construct validity.
issues.quote: The demonstration of the fallibility of memory will be done by means of the DRM technique... Demonstrating the individual fallibility of memory should make the participants alert to the real possibility that their reports may be distorted as a result of a discussion with the partner.

issues.description: The manuscript specifies that the experimental podcasts are approximately 7 minutes long, but it does not report the length of the podcast used in the control condition. Without this information, it is impossible to evaluate whether the control condition adequately matches the experimental conditions in terms of time delay and cognitive engagement.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The authors state that in previous studies, the warning was placed after the collaborative recall. In the very next sentence, they state that in the present study, they 'decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall,' implying this is a specific, potentially novel design choice requiring rationale, which contradicts the preceding sentence stating this is the standard approach.
issues.quote: In all the aforementioned studies the warning was placed after the collaborative recall... In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall (see the rationale for the research below).

issues.description: The analysis plan includes an index for 'answers consistent with the misinformation.' However, for non-discussed items, no misinformation was actually presented during the collaborative recall. The manuscript does not explicitly explain how this index is calculated for non-discussed items (e.g., whether it refers to answers consistent with the alternate version of the movie that the partner saw but did not discuss).
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation...

issues.description: The authors state specific, ordered hypotheses regarding the relative efficacy of the three interventions (Demonstration > Extended Warning > Education). However, the analysis plan only specifies generic 'follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups' following a significant omnibus interaction. They should pre-specify planned contrasts to directly test their ordered hypotheses, rather than relying on omnibus tests and post-hoc pairwise comparisons, which reduces power and increases analytic flexibility.
issues.quote: we tentatively assume that the most effective technique... will be Demonstration and motivation... Extended warning... is expected to be slightly less effective than Demonstration... but more effective than Education... In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.description: It is not specified whether the interventions (Phase 3) are administered to participants individually or while they are still sitting together as a pair. This is particularly problematic for the 'Demonstration and motivation' condition, where participants complete a DRM recall task. If they complete this task in the presence of their partner, social influence could affect their DRM performance, confounding the demonstration of individual memory fallibility.
issues.quote: After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation... The participants will be randomly divided into four groups...

issues.description: The authors state that excluded participants will be 'replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size.' Because the core manipulation (collaborative recall) occurs in interacting dyads, it is impossible to replace a single participant without either running a completely new pair (thus replacing two people) or using a confederate, which is not mentioned. This indicates a flaw in understanding dyadic data collection.
issues.quote: If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size.

issues.description: The authors state that the age of participants in each pair will be matched 'as far as possible.' This is too vague for a pre-registered protocol or reproducible method. They need to specify the maximum allowable age difference between partners in a dyad.
issues.quote: In addition, the age of the participants in each pair will be matched as far as possible.

issues.description: The reference list includes a citation for 'Condon, C. E., Ritchie, T. D., & Igou, E. R. (2015)' but this paper is never cited in the main text of the manuscript.
issues.quote: Condon, C. E., Ritchie, T. D., & Igou, E. R. (2015). How dyads reminiscence moderates the relations between familiarity, trust, and memory conformity. Social Psychology, 46(2), 65–75.

issues.description: The reference list includes 'Gabbert, F., Memon, A., & Allan, K. (2003)' but this source is not cited anywhere in the manuscript text.
issues.quote: Gabbert, F., Memon, A., & Allan, K. (2003). Memory conformity: Can eyewitnesses influence each other’s memories for an event? Applied Cognitive Psychology, 17(5), 533–543.

issues.subcategory: Missing analysis plan for collected data
issues.description: The procedure states that participants will rate their subjective certainty for each answer on a 0-100% scale. However, the analysis plan does not mention how or if this certainty data will be analyzed. Collecting data without a pre-specified analysis plan introduces analytic flexibility (e.g., researchers might later decide to use certainty as a covariate or moderator without pre-registration).
issues.quote: Moreover, for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty).

issues.description: The analysis plan states that the researchers will 'observe' the average accuracy on filler questions. It is unclear what statistical tests, if any, will be performed on these items, what the hypotheses are, or how these results will be interpreted. This vague language leaves room for undisclosed researcher degrees of freedom.
issues.quote: Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.description: In the 'Demonstration and motivation' condition, the DRM task is used to demonstrate individual memory fallibility. The experimenter tells participants they were 'fooled' if they wrote down specific critical lures. However, the DRM effect does not occur for 100% of participants. The protocol does not specify what feedback is given or how the manipulation is handled if a participant does not falsely recall any of the critical lures, which would mean the demonstration of their individual vulnerability failed.
issues.quote: See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief. If so, you were fooled... You can see how easily human memory can be distorted

issues.description: The fourth index derived from the memory test is 'the overall number of answers.' It is unclear what this means. It could mean the total number of questions attempted (vs. left blank or answered 'I don't know'), or it could be the sum of the first three indices. If it is a linear combination of the other indices, running a separate ANOVA on it is redundant and statistically inappropriate.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers... and (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.description: The power analysis for the main memory conformity effect averages two highly disparate effect sizes (g = 1.92 and g = 0.38) using a random effects model to yield an expected effect size of 1.13. Estimating a random effects meta-analytic mean with only two studies is highly unstable. By powering for a very large effect (1.13) rather than the more conservative estimate (0.38), the study risks being severely underpowered to detect the main effect if the true effect size is closer to the smaller estimate.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92... and Hedges’ g = 0.38... random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.description: The three experimental conditions have heavily overlapping content, undermining their construct validity as distinct interventions. 'Demonstration and motivation' includes explicit instructions to 'only use information that they remember' (which is a warning). 'Extended warning' includes an 'extensive lecture on the nature of the misinformation effect' (which is education). Because the conditions share active ingredients (warnings and education), comparing them cannot cleanly isolate the mechanisms of resistance.
issues.quote: [Demonstration] They will also be instructed that if they ever testify as a witness, they should only use information that they remember... [Extended warning] an extensive lecture on the nature of the misinformation effect...

issues.description: The control group listens to a podcast about 'soft skills related to social attitudes.' Because memory conformity is driven by social influence and social compliance, a podcast about social attitudes might inadvertently prime social conformity or alter social behavior, acting as an active manipulation rather than a neutral baseline. A neutral educational topic (e.g., history or astronomy) would be a more appropriate control for the memory education podcasts.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The procedure includes two filler tasks (15 minutes of logic puzzles and 5 minutes of multiplication problems) completed while participants are presumably still sitting together. The protocol does not specify whether participants are allowed to talk or interact during these filler tasks. Uncontrolled social interaction can build rapport, which is known to moderate memory conformity.
issues.quote: After watching the video, the participants will be engaged in a filler task (solving logic puzzles) for 15 minutes... After the discussion, there will be another filler task: the participants will be asked to work on multiplication problems for five minutes.

issues.description: The study equates 'discussed items' with 'misinformation exposure.' However, the coding scheme acknowledges that during a discussion, a partner might 'not give an answer' or might agree with the participant. In these cases, the participant is not exposed to any contradictory information from the co-witness. Treating all 'discussed' items as 'misinformation' items in the ANOVA will dilute the effect and misrepresent the construct of misinformation exposure.
issues.quote: if Participant A gave an answer... and Participant B agreed with it or did not give an answer it will be classified as “non-disputed”... analyzing memory conformity is based on a within-subjects factor... (discussed vs. non-discussed items)

issues.description: The use of open-ended questions allows participants to provide complex answers, such as reporting both the original detail and the co-witness detail, or explicitly stating the source of their memory (e.g., 'I saw X but my partner said Y'). The proposed scoring system (correct, misinformation, other) does not specify how such compound or source-explicit responses will be coded, leaving room for subjective interpretation and analytic flexibility.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers...
